Add a 1.2 MW unity-power-factor PV unit at bus 61, keep the original loads unchanged, run a balanced AC power flow, and report the active power imported from the upstream source at bus 1 in MW, with positive meaning power supplied into the feeder.
reference_code:
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Canonical Baran-Wu IEEE 69-bus radial distribution feeder (frozen artifact).

Why this file exists
--------------------
E4 layer-2b' query A02 asks for "the canonical Baran-Wu IEEE 69-bus radial
distribution feeder, with bus numbers referring to the published 1-69 labels and
with the exact base-case data frozen with the benchmark".  pandapower 3.4.0 has
no built-in 69-bus feeder (``pandapower.networks`` ships case4gs/5/6ww/9/14/30/
case_ieee30/33bw/39/57/89pegase/118/145/... but nothing 69-bus), so the network
data is pinned here and frozen together with the query set.  This is an
artifact-pinning requirement stated by the engineer-approved README; it is NOT a
change to the approved engineering request.

Data provenance
---------------
M. E. Baran and F. F. Wu, "Optimal capacitor placement on radial distribution
systems", IEEE Trans. Power Delivery 4(1):725-734, 1989 -- the 69-bus
(sometimes "70-bus" incl. the source node) feeder, in the widely reproduced
base-case tabulation: 69 buses, 68 series branches, nominal 12.66 kV, branch
resistance/reactance in ohms, spot loads in kW/kvar attached to the receiving
("to") bus of each branch.  Tie branches used in reconfiguration studies are NOT
part of the base case and are not created here (the base case is strictly
radial, as the query requires).

Totals implied by the table below (checked by ``sanity_check``):
    sum P = 3801.89 kW,  sum Q = 2694.10 kvar
Some papers quote 3802.19 kW / 2694.60 kvar for a near-identical variant of the
same feeder (+0.30 kW / +0.50 kvar); the tabulation frozen here is internally
consistent and is the one the benchmark is defined against.

Reference base-case results reproduced by this implementation (slack 1.0 p.u.
at bus label 1) -- these are the standard published check values for the feeder:
    total active loss ~ 225 kW,  min bus voltage ~ 0.9092 p.u. at bus label 65.

Bus labelling convention (E4 layer-2b' README rule)
---------------------------------------------------
Published labels are 1..69.  pandapower table indices are 0-based; this builder
creates bus label ``n`` at pandapower bus index ``n - 1`` and also writes the
label into ``net.bus['name']`` as ``"Bus <n>"``.  Use ``bus_index(label)`` to
convert.  No other mapping is implied anywhere in the benchmark.

Ratings note
------------
The published data set specifies only R, X and the spot loads.  Line current
ratings are not published; ``MAX_I_KA`` below is an implementation constant
(uniform, non-binding: the base case and query A02 draw <= ~0.19 kA at the
feeder head).  Shunt capacitance is zero, as in the published data.

Frozen: 2026-07-30 with ``e4_layer2b_set.json``.  Everything above the
END-FROZEN-BUILDER marker is embedded verbatim in the reference_code of A02, so
the query set is self-contained and the sha256 of this file pins the network.
"""

VN_KV = 12.66

def bus_index(label):
    """Published 1-based bus label -> 0-based pandapower bus table index."""
    return label - 1


def create_ieee69_baran_wu():
    """Build the canonical Baran-Wu IEEE 69-bus radial feeder (base case)."""
    net = pp.create_empty_network(name="IEEE 69-bus Baran-Wu radial feeder")
    for label in range(1, 70):
        pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=VN_KV, name="Bus %d" % label, index=label - 1)
    pp.create_ext_grid(net, bus=SLACK_LABEL - 1, vm_pu=1.0, va_degree=0.0,
                       name="Substation")
    for f, t, r, x, p_kw, q_kvar in BARAN_WU_69_BRANCHES:
        pp.create_line_from_parameters(
            net, from_bus=f - 1, to_bus=t - 1, length_km=1.0,
            r_ohm_per_km=r, x_ohm_per_km=x, c_nf_per_km=0.0,
            max_i_ka=MAX_I_KA, name="Line %d-%d" % (f, t))
        if p_kw != 0.0 or q_kvar != 0.0:
            pp.create_load(net, bus=t - 1, p_mw=p_kw / 1000.0,
                           q_mvar=q_kvar / 1000.0, name="Load %d" % t)
    return net

net = create_ieee69_baran_wu()
pp.create_sgen(net, bus=bus_index(61), p_mw=1.2, q_mvar=0.0)
pp.runpp(net)
print(round(float(net.res_ext_grid.p_mw.iloc[0]), 6))

Sweep its reactive-power setpoint from −2000 to +2000 kvar in 1 kvar increments, run a balanced AC power flow at each setpoint, and select the converged setpoint that minimizes the absolute deviation of the bus-18 voltage from 1.000 p.u.; if tied, choose the smaller numerical setpoint. import pandapower as pp
import pandapower.networks as pn
net = pn.case33bw()
b = 18 - 1
sid = pp.create_sgen(net, bus=b, p_mw=0.400, q_mvar=0.0)
best_q = None
best_dev = None
for q_kvar in range(-2000, 2001):
    net.sgen.at[sid, 'q_mvar'] = q_kvar / 1000.0
    try:
        pp.runpp(net)
    except Exception:
        continue
    if not bool(net.converged):
        continue
    dev = abs(float(net.res_bus.vm_pu.at[b]) - 1.0)
    if best_dev is None or dev < best_dev:
        best_dev = dev
        best_q = q_kvar
print(best_q)

natural_language_query: Use the CIGRE LV benchmark and identify residential loads as the existing load elements whose names begin with “Load R.” At each residential load bus, add a unity-power-factor PV unit whose rated active power equals that load’s original active power, then independently solve two balanced AC power-flow scenarios in which every original load and every added PV are scaled by (0.45, 0.90) and (0.80, 0.20), respectively. Report the highest voltage magnitude over all in-service 0.4 kV buses and both scenarios.
reference_code:
import pandapower as pp
import pandapower.networks as pn

def scenario(load_scale, pv_scale):
    net = pn.create_cigre_network_lv()
    residential = [i for i in net.load.index
                   if str(net.load.name.at[i]).startswith('Load R')]
    for li in residential:
        pp.create_sgen(net, bus=int(net.load.bus.at[li]),
                       p_mw=float(net.load.p_mw.at[li]) * pv_scale, q_mvar=0.0)
    net.load['p_mw'] = net.load['p_mw'] * load_scale
    net.load['q_mvar'] = net.load['q_mvar'] * load_scale
    pp.runpp(net)
    mask = (net.bus['vn_kv'] == 0.4) & net.bus['in_service']
    return float(net.res_bus.vm_pu[mask].max())

print(round(max(scenario(0.45, 0.80), scenario(0.90, 0.20)), 5))

natural_language_query: Use the CIGRE MV benchmark without DER and close the three normally open line switches S1, S2, and S3, leaving all other statuses unchanged. Run a balanced AC power flow, select the in-service line with the highest loading percentage, breaking an exact tie by the smallest line-record index, take that line out of service, and rerun the power flow. Define total active-power loss as the sum over all in-service lines and transformers, and report 100 × (post-outage loss − pre-outage loss) / pre-outage loss.
reference_code:
import pandapower as pp
import pandapower.networks as pn

def total_loss_mw(net):
    line = float(net.res_line.loc[net.line.in_service, 'pl_mw'].sum())
    trafo = float(net.res_trafo.loc[net.trafo.in_service, 'pl_mw'].sum())
    return line + trafo

net = pn.create_cigre_network_mv(with_der=False)
for si in net.switch.index:
    if str(net.switch.name.at[si]) in ('S1', 'S2', 'S3'):
        net.switch.at[si, 'closed'] = True
pp.runpp(net)
pre = total_loss_mw(net)
loading = net.res_line.loc[net.line.in_service, 'loading_percent']
worst = max(loading.index, key=lambda i: (float(loading.at[i]), -int(i)))
net.line.at[worst, 'in_service'] = False
pp.runpp(net)
post = total_loss_mw(net)
print(round(100.0 * (post - pre) / pre, 4))

import pandapower as pp
import pandapower.networks as pn
from pandapower.topology import create_nxgraph

natural_language_query: Use the built-in IEEE 57-bus case and test λ = 1.00, 1.01, …, 2.00 in ascending order; at each value multiply every load’s active and reactive demand by λ, retain the base active-power and voltage setpoints of all non-slack generators, enforce their original reactive-power limits, and let the external grid balance the system. For each λ, test the 62 single-line outages whose individual removal leaves the original network connected, keeping all transformers in service; a value fails if any contingency power flow does not converge, any in-service bus voltage lies outside 0.95–1.05 p.u., or any remaining line’s larger terminal-current-to-rated-current ratio exceeds 100%. Return the largest passing λ, return 0.00 if λ = 1.00 fails, and return 2.00 if every tested value passes.
reference_code:
import pandapower as pp
import pandapower.networks as pn
from pandapower.topology import create_nxgraph
import networkx as nx
base = pn.case57()
base_cc = nx.number_connected_components(create_nxgraph(base, respect_switches=True))
eligible = []
for li in list(base.line.index[base.line.in_service]):
    base.line.at[li, 'in_service'] = False
    if nx.number_connected_components(create_nxgraph(base, respect_switches=True)) == base_cc:
        eligible.append(int(li))
    base.line.at[li, 'in_service'] = True
base_p = base.load['p_mw'].copy()
base_q = base.load['q_mvar'].copy()

def passes(lam):
    for li in eligible:
        net = pn.case57()
        net.load['p_mw'] = base_p * lam
        net.load['q_mvar'] = base_q * lam
        net.line.at[li, 'in_service'] = False
        try:
            pp.runpp(net, enforce_q_lims=True)
        except Exception:
            return False
        if not bool(net.converged):
            return False
        vm = net.res_bus.vm_pu[net.bus.in_service]
        if float(vm.min()) < 0.95 or float(vm.max()) > 1.05:
            return False
        imax = net.res_line[['i_from_ka', 'i_to_ka']].max(axis=1)
        loading = (imax / net.line.loc[imax.index, 'max_i_ka'] * 100.0)[net.line.in_service]
        if float(loading.max()) > 100.0:
            return False
    return True

lams = [round(1.00 + 0.01 * k, 2) for k in range(101)]
passing = [lam for lam in lams if passes(lam)]
if 1.00 not in passing:
    answer = 0.00
elif len(passing) == len(lams):
    answer = 2.00
else:
    answer = max(passing)
print(round(answer, 2))

natural_language_query: Use the built-in IEEE 118-bus case and run a base AC power flow, then select the online non-slack generator with the largest active-power output, breaking a tie by the smallest bus label and then the smallest generator-record index. Take that generator out of service and redistribute its pre-contingency MW once among the remaining online non-slack generators in proportion to each unit’s upward reserve, defined as original maximum active power minus base active-power output; exclude the external grid at bus 69 from this allocation and let it supply only losses and numerical allocation residual. Keep the remaining generators’ original voltage setpoints, enforce their original reactive-power limits, rerun the AC power flow, and report the greatest loading among line elements only, defined as the larger terminal-current magnitude divided by rated current.
reference_code:
import pandapower as pp
import pandapower.networks as pn
net = pn.case118()
pp.runpp(net)
online = [int(g) for g in net.gen.index if bool(net.gen.in_service.at[g])]
p_base = net.res_gen['p_mw']
worst = max(online, key=lambda g: (float(p_base.at[g]),
                                   -(int(net.gen.bus.at[g]) + 1), -int(g)))
p_lost = float(p_base.at[worst])
net.gen.at[worst, 'in_service'] = False
remaining = [g for g in online if g != worst]
reserve = {g: max(0.0, float(net.gen.max_p_mw.at[g]) - float(net.gen.p_mw.at[g]))
           for g in remaining}
total_reserve = sum(reserve.values())
for g in remaining:
    net.gen.at[g, 'p_mw'] = float(net.gen.p_mw.at[g]) + p_lost * reserve[g] / total_reserve
pp.runpp(net, enforce_q_lims=True)
imax = net.res_line[['i_from_ka', 'i_to_ka']].max(axis=1)
loading = (imax / net.line.loc[imax.index, 'max_i_ka'] * 100.0)[net.line.in_service]
print(round(float(loading.max()), 4))

Use the load-reference sign convention for bus injections and exclude fixed-shunt consumption from those measurements because the shunt remains represented in the network admittance; use the power-flow values without noise except for adding 0.03 p.u. to the Bus 14 voltage measurement, with standard deviations of 0.005 p.u., 1 MW, and 1 Mvar for voltage, active power, and reactive power, respectively. Run flat-start weighted least-squares state estimation and report the estimated Bus 14 voltage magnitude.
reference_code:
import pandapower as pp
import pandapower.networks as pn
from pandapower.estimation import estimate
STD_V, STD_P, STD_Q = 0.005, 1.0, 1.0
net = pn.case14()
pp.runpp(net)
shunt_p, shunt_q = {}, {}
for si in net.shunt.index:
    b = int(net.shunt.bus.at[si])
    shunt_p[b] = shunt_p.get(b, 0.0) + float(net.res_shunt.p_mw.at[si])
    shunt_q[b] = shunt_q.get(b, 0.0) + float(net.res_shunt.q_mvar.at[si])
for b in net.bus.index:
    v = float(net.res_bus.vm_pu.at[b]) + (0.03 if int(b) == 14 - 1 else 0.0)
    pp.create_measurement(net, 'v', 'bus', v, STD_V, element=int(b))
for b in net.bus.index:
    p = float(net.res_bus.p_mw.at[b]) - shunt_p.get(int(b), 0.0)
    q = float(net.res_bus.q_mvar.at[b]) - shunt_q.get(int(b), 0.0)
    pp.create_measurement(net, 'p', 'bus', p, STD_P, element=int(b))
    pp.create_measurement(net, 'q', 'bus', q, STD_Q, element=int(b))
for li in net.line.index:
    pp.create_measurement(net, 'p', 'line', float(net.res_line.p_from_mw.at[li]),
                          STD_P, element=int(li), side='from')
    pp.create_measurement(net, 'q', 'line', float(net.res_line.q_from_mvar.at[li]),
                          STD_Q, element=int(li), side='from')
for ti in net.trafo.index:
    pp.create_measurement(net, 'p', 'trafo', float(net.res_trafo.p_hv_mw.at[ti]),
                          STD_P, element=int(ti), side='hv')
    pp.create_measurement(net, 'q', 'trafo', float(net.res_trafo.q_hv_mvar.at[ti]),
                          STD_Q, element=int(ti), side='hv')
estimate(net, init='flat')
print(round(float(net.res_bus_est.vm_pu.at[14 - 1]), 6))

import pandapower.networks as pn
reference = pn.case14()
base_p = reference.load['p_mw'].copy()
base_q = reference.load['q_mvar'].copy()
answer = 5.00
for k in range(401):
    lam = round(1.00 + 0.01 * k, 2)
    net = pn.case14()
    net.load['p_mw'] = base_p * lam
    net.load['q_mvar'] = base_q * lam
    failed = False
    try:
        pp.runpp(net, algorithm='nr', init='flat', max_iteration=50,
                 enforce_q_lims=True)
        if not bool(net.converged) or float(net.res_bus.vm_pu.min()) < 0.70:
            failed = True
    except Exception:
        failed = True
    if failed:
        answer = round(lam - 0.01, 2)
        break
